title: Compare task retry with a shared update
question: Which progress survives a local retry, and which waits for every required contribution?
scope: Separate three-map and three-worker toy jobs. Schematic lane positions indicate dependencies; panel steps are pedagogical inspections, not synchronized wall-clock samples. Map outputs and scalar gradients are illustrative; optimizer learning rate is one sixth.

steps.title: Establish the two dependency patterns
steps.explanation: The panels are separate illustrative jobs. Their lanes show dependency ordering, not a shared clock across panels.

snapshot.result: The map job retains independent records; the training job must eventually commit one shared update.

steps.title: Fail only map 3’s first attempt
steps.explanation: The scheduler retries the failed task. Maps 1 and 2 continue toward completion without restarting.

snapshot.result: Only the failed attempt is retried. Other maps continue; no completed task is invalidated.

transition.meaning: Record one map failure and activate only its retry.

steps.title: Finish maps 1 and 2 independently
steps.explanation: Their output records persist even though map 3 and the dependent reducer have not completed.

snapshot.result: Maps 1 and 2 have durable-in-this-scene output records; map 3 cannot erase their completed work.

transition.meaning: Complete two independent map tasks in parallel.

steps.title: Finish the retry of map 3
steps.explanation: The reducer can now run because every map output it requires exists.

snapshot.result: The missing record now exists, so the dependent reducer becomes runnable.

transition.meaning: Complete the retried map and satisfy the reducer dependency.

steps.title: Finish the dependent reducer
steps.explanation: Local retry preserved other tasks’ progress, but the missing map output still delayed this reducer.

snapshot.result: The reducer finishes from the retained records; independent map completion did not remove its dependencies.

transition.meaning: Compute the reducer from all three retained records.

steps.title: Finish gradients 0 and 1
steps.explanation: Healthy workers retain their contributions and wait. The old weight remains in place while worker 2 is late.

snapshot.result: Healthy workers have finished local work, but the missing third contribution holds the shared weight unchanged.

transition.meaning: Complete the two healthy gradient tasks in parallel.

steps.title: Finish the last required gradient
steps.explanation: The complete contribution set now permits AllReduce; gradient readiness itself is not the shared parameter update.

snapshot.result: All contributions now exist; the collective may run, while the old shared weight is still retained.

transition.meaning: Complete the late gradient and release the collective dependency.

steps.title: Finish the shared AllReduce
steps.explanation: The scalar collective returns the sum of all contributions. The old shared weight still remains until optimizer commit.

snapshot.result: The complete collective result is ready; the optimizer commit remains a separate dependency.

transition.meaning: Complete the collective reduction of all required contributions.

steps.title: Commit the shared weight update
steps.explanation: The toy optimizer uses learning rate one sixth. This update cannot omit the late worker’s gradient.

snapshot.result: Every required contribution is included in the new shared weight.

transition.meaning: Complete the shared optimizer update after the collective.

invariants: A failed map does not invalidate completed output records from other maps.
A reducer still waits for every map output it depends on.
The synchronous shared update requires every worker contribution and the completed collective.
The shared weight remains unchanged while any required gradient is missing.

title: Follow one tensor through the sending node
question: Which memory traffic disappears when the NIC reads GPU memory directly?
scope: Toy sending-node transfer of an 8-byte payload. Count only payload writes and reads at host memory; exclude protocol headers, transactions, receiving-node traffic, and hardware timing.

steps.title: Retain the source tensor
steps.explanation: The same tensor T is used in both declared paths.

snapshot.result: The source tensor is retained in GPU memory; no host bounce or fabric transfer has occurred.

steps.title: Write T into registered host memory
steps.explanation: This payload write contributes one payload length of host-memory traffic.

snapshot.result: A host copy now exists alongside the original GPU tensor; this host write is the first bounce cost.

transition.meaning: Stage a copy without consuming the GPU source.

steps.title: Read the host copy into the NIC
steps.explanation: The NIC read adds a second payload length of host-memory traffic.

snapshot.result: The NIC has read the retained host copy; host traffic includes both a payload write and a payload read.

transition.meaning: Read the retained host copy.

steps.title: Send T onto the fabric
steps.explanation: The fabric carries the same tensor as the direct path.

snapshot.result: The full tensor still traverses the fabric; avoiding the host bounce does not remove network payload.

transition.meaning: Transmit the full payload.

invariants: Reads preserve the source tensor and any retained host copy.
Both paths send the same payload onto the network.
Removing host staging does not change the physical network rate.

variants.label: GPUDirect peer path
variants.scope: Same tensor, direct NIC read from GPU memory; identical host and fabric accounting.

steps.title: Retain the source tensor
steps.explanation: The same tensor T is used in both declared paths.

snapshot.result: The source tensor is retained in GPU memory; no host bounce or fabric transfer has occurred.

steps.title: Read GPU memory into the NIC
steps.explanation: The PCIe peer path bypasses the registered host buffer.

snapshot.result: The NIC has a copy directly from GPU memory. The host buffer remains empty.

transition.meaning: Read GPU memory without consuming its tensor.

steps.title: Send T onto the fabric
steps.explanation: The network still carries the full payload.

snapshot.result: The full tensor still traverses the fabric; avoiding the host bounce does not remove network payload.

transition.meaning: Transmit one payload; retain the sender copy.

steps.title: Release the completed NIC staging slot
steps.explanation: The fabric has accepted the payload; the source GPU tensor remains retained.

snapshot.result: The completed send no longer needs its NIC slot. The GPU source tensor remains available.

transition.meaning: Release the completed send buffer.

title: Break a cyclic buffer dependency
question: Why do full queues and upstream PAUSE prevent every packet from advancing?
scope: Four queues with one packet slot each, abstracting the full queues in the figure. Initial packets require the next queue clockwise. One explicit watchdog drop and one subsequent hop are shown; no timer, retransmission, or hardware policy is modeled.

steps.title: Begin with one free downstream slot
steps.explanation: Each packet requires the next queue clockwise. The toy queue capacity is one packet.

snapshot.result: One queue still has downstream space; the occupied dependency cycle has not closed.

steps.title: Fill the last queue
steps.explanation: P4 closes the occupied dependency cycle; no packet has downstream space.

snapshot.result: Every queue is occupied by a packet needing the next full queue; none has a free destination.

transition.meaning: Enqueue P4 into the final free slot.

steps.title: Assert PAUSE toward every upstream predecessor
steps.explanation: Each full queue pauses its predecessor. All four packets remain resident and none can drain.

snapshot.result: The clockwise waiting cycle and counterclockwise PAUSE messages hold every resident packet.

transition.meaning: Emit one parallel round of upstream PAUSE control messages.

steps.title: Drop P1 under the declared watchdog policy
steps.explanation: The external watchdog deliberately sacrifices one packet to open space; transport recovery is outside this scene.

snapshot.result: The watchdog opens one slot by losing a packet. That loss is a recovery cost, not delivery.

transition.meaning: Watchdog drops P1 rather than delivering it.

steps.title: Clear b1’s PAUSE toward b4
steps.explanation: Space alone does not override a still-active PAUSE. Queue b1 now allows its upstream neighbor to send.

pause.status: b1 has space and clears its PAUSE toward b4

snapshot.result: Queue b4 may send into b1 because both downstream space and PAUSE clearance now exist.

transition.meaning: Clear only the PAUSE emitted by b1.

steps.title: Forward P4 from b4 into the freed slot
steps.explanation: One packet advances clockwise. Further PAUSE clearance and reliable recovery follow outside this bounded scene.

pause.status: Earlier PAUSE clearance allowed b4 to forward; later controls are outside this scene

snapshot.result: P4 advances into b1 and frees b4. Breaking one dependency permits forward progress.

transition.meaning: Forward P4 after downstream space and PAUSE clearance.

invariants: PAUSE travels upstream, opposite to the packet-forwarding dependency.
No packet leaves a full cycle before the external watchdog drop.
Resident packets plus deliberate drops equal all packets admitted; a drop is not successful delivery.

title: Watch the prefetch queue drain
question: When does overlap stop hiding storage and preparation latency?
scope: Focused warm pipeline with three batches B1–B3 and one prepared queue slot. B1 warm-up is omitted. Shared schematic intervals explicitly model one delayed B3 read; they are a supplementary variance case rather than the static figure’s four-batch throughput comparison.

objects.label: Read, prepare, and train batch identities

steps.title: Inspect three batch identities in flight
steps.explanation: GPU trains B1, CPU prepares B2, and storage reads B3. Initial warm-up of B1 is outside this focused scene.

done.status: No batch completed in this scene

snapshot.result: Three different batches occupy three stages concurrently; the GPU still needs a prepared successor.

steps.title: Finish preparing B2 into the ready queue
steps.explanation: The prepared batch waits in host memory while the GPU finishes B1; overlap does not merge batch identities.

done.status: No batch completed in this scene

snapshot.result: B2 waits ready in the prefetch queue while B1 continues on the GPU.

transition.meaning: Prepare one raw batch and retain its ready representation.

steps.title: Finish GPU training on B1
steps.explanation: B1’s completed record remains visible. The already prepared B2 is ready for dispatch.

snapshot.result: B1 is complete and B2 remains queued, so the GPU has a prepared successor.

transition.meaning: Complete GPU work on batch B1.

steps.title: Dispatch the queued B2 to the GPU
steps.explanation: Dispatch consumes the one queued prepared batch. Storage is still reading delayed B3.

gpu.status: B2 dispatched from the ready queue

snapshot.result: B2 runs on the GPU, leaving no prepared batch in reserve for the delayed B3 read.

transition.meaning: Move the prepared batch to its GPU consumer.

steps.title: Finish B2 and expose an empty input queue
steps.explanation: The prefetch cushion is exhausted before B3 arrives. No useful GPU computation can continue.

snapshot.result: B2 is complete, but B3 is still upstream. Empty prefetch capacity cannot supply useful GPU work.

transition.meaning: Complete GPU work on B2; the next required batch is absent.

steps.title: Finish delayed storage delivery of B3
steps.explanation: B3 is raw data, so arrival alone cannot resume the GPU. CPU preparation remains a dependency.

snapshot.result: B3 has arrived as raw data. The GPU must still wait for CPU preparation.

transition.meaning: Complete one read and deliver its raw batch.

steps.title: Finish preparing B3
steps.explanation: The newly ready batch ends exposed input wait, but dispatch remains an explicit next action.

snapshot.result: B3 is finally prepared; the exposed input gap ends when the GPU dispatches this ready batch.

transition.meaning: Finish CPU preparation of the required next batch.

steps.title: Dispatch B3 and resume GPU training
steps.explanation: Prefetching hid earlier delivery work, but the delayed read and preparation exposed a real gap once the queue drained.

snapshot.result: The GPU resumes with B3. Prefetching hid earlier delivery work only until its reserve drained.

transition.meaning: Move B3 from ready storage into its GPU consumer.

invariants: The GPU consumes only prepared batches, never raw read output.
Batch identity persists through read, preparation, queueing, and GPU consumption.
Queue dispatch removes a prepared batch from the queue.
An empty queue with unfinished upstream work exposes GPU input wait.

title: Separate staging from checkpoint commitment
question: When can a resumed training run safely restore from the new generation?
scope: Toy two-rank generation g1 captures scalar weight 10 while g0 is already committed. One later training step adds one. Schematic lanes show dependencies rather than measured duration; checksum match is an explicit verification outcome, not a simulated hash algorithm.

steps.title: Pause at a consistent training cut
steps.explanation: The previous committed generation g0 remains the only restore point.

snapshot.result: The consistent cut is paused, and g0 remains the sole committed restore point.

steps.title: Finish immutable local shard writes
steps.explanation: Both shards describe the same consistent cut. Training may now resume, but g1 is not durably committed.

snapshot.result: Immutable g1 shards exist locally. Resuming training does not make this generation restorable.

transition.meaning: Finish parallel local writes from one consistent training cut.

steps.title: Advance live training on its next step
steps.explanation: Live state changes while local g1 shards retain the earlier values used by the checkpoint.

snapshot.result: Live weight advances while staged shards retain the earlier cut; recovery still uses g0.

transition.meaning: Complete one live training step while the immutable copy source is retained.

steps.title: Finish the durable copy of rank 0’s shard
steps.explanation: A completed shard copy is durable data, not a published checkpoint.

snapshot.result: Only one g1 shard is durable. Publishing this incomplete generation would expose a broken restore point.

transition.meaning: Persist one immutable shard without consuming local staging.

steps.title: Finish the durable copy of rank 1’s shard
steps.explanation: A completed shard copy is durable data, not a published checkpoint.

snapshot.result: Both g1 shards are durable, but verification and manifest publication still precede commitment.

transition.meaning: Persist one immutable shard without consuming local staging.

steps.title: Verify every required shard
steps.explanation: The coordinator checks the complete shard set before publication. The restore pointer still names g0.

verified.status: Every persisted shard matches its declared checksum

snapshot.result: The full shard set is verified. The restore pointer remains g0 until the atomic manifest commit.

transition.meaning: Verify the two shard checksums as one parallel verification operation.

steps.title: Publish the g1 manifest atomically
steps.explanation: Only the manifest commit makes g1 the declared restore point; staged data alone never changes that pointer.

verified.status: Every persisted shard matches its declared checksum

snapshot.result: The committed manifest now names complete g1, so the restore point can advance safely.

transition.meaning: Atomically publish the complete verified generation.

steps.title: Release local staging after publication
steps.explanation: The durable complete generation is committed and no modeled consumer still needs the local shards.

verified.status: Every persisted shard matches its declared checksum

snapshot.result: Local staging is free only after durable copies and publication have finished using it.

transition.meaning: Free local staging after its copy and commit obligations.

invariants: Every g1 shard belongs to the same immutable consistent cut.
Live training cannot mutate an already staged g1 shard.
The restore pointer remains g0 until all g1 shards are durable, verified, and named by the atomic manifest.
No local staging slot is released before copy completion and manifest publication.

title: Expose the final communication tail
question: Which transfer is hidden by backward work, and which still delays the update?
scope: Focused final two layers L2 and L1 of the four-layer diagram; earlier layers are complete. Backward tasks and transfers each take three schematic units; each launch occupies the GPU for one. No measured speedup is claimed. The toy final weight decrement is one.

objects.label: Final backward layers and their AllReduce

steps.title: Begin the final two backward layers
steps.explanation: Earlier layers L4 and L3 from the source diagram are outside this focused scene and already complete.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: L2 backward is still producing its gradient; neither final-layer collective can run yet.

steps.title: Finish backward L2
steps.explanation: The local L2 gradient becomes available. Its collective has not launched.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: L2 is locally ready, but launching its transfer still occupies the GPU.

transition.meaning: Complete one backward layer and expose its gradient.

steps.title: Finish L2’s nonoverlappable launch overhead
steps.explanation: The GPU has paid the launch overhead; network L2 can run while GPU backward L1 runs.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: Network L2 and GPU backward L1 now use separate engines concurrently.

transition.meaning: Complete the launch overhead and hand off work to concurrent engines.

steps.title: Finish the concurrent L1 backward and L2 transfer
steps.explanation: The declared equal-length interval finishes both parallel tasks. L1 is now ready, but its AllReduce has not launched.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: L2 communication finishes beneath L1 backward. L1’s own transfer is still outstanding.

transition.meaning: Complete the parallel backward/communication interval on separate engines.

steps.title: Finish L1’s nonoverlappable launch overhead
steps.explanation: There is no backward computation left to hide the final transfer. The optimizer still waits for L1.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: L1 transfer now runs with no later backward work to hide it; the optimizer must wait.

transition.meaning: Complete final launch overhead and start the exposed transfer.

steps.title: Finish the exposed L1 AllReduce
steps.explanation: All required reduced gradients are finally available; only now may the optimizer execute.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: The exposed final transfer is complete. All required reduced gradients can now feed the optimizer.

transition.meaning: Complete the final network transfer on the critical path.

steps.title: Complete the optimizer update
steps.explanation: A declared toy optimizer decrement consumes the complete reduced gradient set.

metrics.label: Completed final overhead and network tail

snapshot.result: The shared optimizer state changes only after the residual communication tail has finished.

transition.meaning: Commit one shared optimizer update after the last collective.

invariants: A layer AllReduce starts only after that layer is ready and its GPU launch overhead completes.
L2 transfer overlaps L1 backward on separate engines.
The final L1 launch overhead and transfer have no later backward work to hide behind.
Optimizer state changes only after every required reduced gradient is available.

title: Track shard ownership across the hierarchy
question: How does each GPU reach the full sum while inter-node work stays sharded?
scope: Toy two-node system with two GPUs per node and two scalar shards per rank. Each step completes one logical collective phase; micro-rounds, bytes, bandwidth, and latency are outside the model.

steps.title: Start with four rank contributions
steps.explanation: Each GPU contributes two scalar shards. Corresponding shard indices must be added together.

snapshot.result: Each GPU starts with its own contribution to both indexed shards.

steps.title: ReduceScatter within each node
steps.explanation: A local collective adds corresponding contributions and leaves each GPU responsible for one node-partial shard.

snapshot.result: Each GPU now owns one node-partial shard; the other shard belongs to its local peer.

transition.meaning: Complete the two independent node-local ReduceScatter operations.

steps.title: AllReduce corresponding shards across nodes
steps.explanation: GPU 0 peers combine shard A; GPU 1 peers combine shard B. Each global sum is replicated only across its shard peers.

snapshot.result: Corresponding inter-node peers hold finished sums, but each GPU still lacks its complementary shard.

transition.meaning: Complete one inter-node AllReduce for each disjoint shard.

steps.title: AllGather the finished shards inside each node
steps.explanation: The local AllGather distributes finished sums without adding them again.

snapshot.result: Local copies distribute the complementary finished shard; every GPU now has the full result.

transition.meaning: Copy the complementary finished shard to the other GPU in each node.

invariants: Local reduction adds only contributions from the same node.
Inter-node peers reduce corresponding shard indices, never different shards.
AllGather copies finished sums and performs no additional summation.

title: Follow values around the ring
question: When does a partial chunk become a finished sum, and why does AllGather stop adding?
scope: Four ranks, four scalar chunks A–D per rank, clockwise logical ring with GPU 3 wrapping to GPU 0. Brackets show exact contributing rank IDs. One step is one simultaneous logical ring round; no physical topology or timing is inferred.

steps.title: Start with indexed local contributions
steps.explanation: Every GPU holds A through D. Brackets name the ranks already included in each numeric value.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: Each chunk contains only its local rank’s contribution; no global sum is complete.

steps.title: ReduceScatter round 1
steps.explanation: Each rank sends one partial chunk clockwise; the receiver adds only contributions not already present.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: The received partial adds previously absent ranks to the same chunk index; brackets expose exactly which contributions are included.

transition.meaning: Complete one simultaneous send/receive-and-add ring round.

steps.title: ReduceScatter round 2
steps.explanation: Each rank sends one partial chunk clockwise; the receiver adds only contributions not already present.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: The received partial adds previously absent ranks to the same chunk index; brackets expose exactly which contributions are included.

transition.meaning: Complete one simultaneous send/receive-and-add ring round.

steps.title: ReduceScatter round 3
steps.explanation: Each rank sends one partial chunk clockwise; the receiver adds only contributions not already present.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: Each GPU now owns one complete sum at a different shard index; other resident tiles are still partial.

transition.meaning: Complete one simultaneous send/receive-and-add ring round.

steps.title: AllGather round 1
steps.explanation: Each rank forwards one finished chunk clockwise. Receivers overwrite stale partials with the finished sum; they do not add again.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: Finished sums propagate clockwise and replace stale partials; already finished source chunks remain retained.

transition.meaning: Copy one finished chunk from each rank to its clockwise neighbor.

steps.title: AllGather round 2
steps.explanation: Each rank forwards one finished chunk clockwise. Receivers overwrite stale partials with the finished sum; they do not add again.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: Finished sums propagate clockwise and replace stale partials; already finished source chunks remain retained.

transition.meaning: Copy one finished chunk from each rank to its clockwise neighbor.

steps.title: AllGather round 3
steps.explanation: Each rank forwards one finished chunk clockwise. Receivers overwrite stale partials with the finished sum; they do not add again.

r0.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r1.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r2.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

r3.status: Value [contributing ranks]; green/ready only when all ranks contributed

snapshot.result: Every GPU now holds every finished sum. AllGather copied the sums without adding contributions again.

transition.meaning: Copy one finished chunk from each rank to its clockwise neighbor.

invariants: ReduceScatter combines disjoint contributor sets for the same chunk index.
After three ReduceScatter rounds GPU 0 owns B, GPU 1 owns C, GPU 2 owns D, and GPU 3 owns A as finished sums.
AllGather copies fully reduced chunks; it never adds a finished sum to an old partial.
Each rank sends one chunk per round and retains the full replicated sum at completion.
